SMTO-SKL-0015 — SMTO couldn't find that Google calendar

GUID: 6b1531f0-c318-5954-9ce8-323a36472b58
Slug: google-calendar-calendar-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: google-calendar

What happened

  • Google says this calendar doesn't exist or this account can't see it. It may have been deleted, unshared, or SMTO used the wrong account. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list your calendars and which Google account it used. The list shows the exact calendars that account can reach, so you can see whether this one is missing.
  2. If the calendar belongs to someone else, open Google Calendar in your browser and check it's still shared with this account. Ask the owner to share it again if not. A calendar that's no longer shared with you looks like it doesn't exist to SMTO.
  3. Pick the right calendar from SMTO's list, or name the right account, and ask for the task again. SMTO needs the exact calendar, and it won't pick a different one with a similar name on its own.

What success looks like

  • The calendar appears in SMTO's calendar list and the task completes on it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the calendar's owner or the person who manages SMTO. Don't create a new calendar with the same name as a replacement; it won't have the original's events or sharing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google returned 404 or 410 for a calendar-scoped Calendar request: the calendar_id does not exist or is not accessible to the selected account.

What this means

  • Google returns HTTP 404 or 410 for a calendar-scoped request. This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Google returns HTTP 404 or 410 for a calendar-scoped request.

How to diagnose it

  • Verify exact calendar_id and account visibility; the response does not prove deletion.

How to fix it

  • Verify the exact calendar_id and the account_ref used. List google_calendar.calendars (requires the calendar_list feature) to see the calendars that account can reach; the calendar may be deleted, unshared or owned by another account.
  • Verify the exact calendar_id and selected account. Inspect google_calendar.calendars when calendar_list access is granted; the calendar may be inaccessible.

Retry and execution caution

  • Verify the exact calendar_id and selected account. Inspect google_calendar.calendars when calendar_list access is granted; the calendar may be inaccessible.

How to verify the fix

  • An authorized read finds the intended calendar under that account.

What not to do

  • Do not expose credentials or private Calendar content in diagnostics.
  • Do not blindly repeat writes after uncertain provider effects.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic performs no provider access. The exact failing stage and retained receipt determine whether a request was sent; account, file or event identity must not be substituted during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
